t: Poland re-emerged as a sovereign state in 1918, and its borders were fixed only after a series of wars from 1918 to 1921, above all the Polish–Soviet War, which ended in a decisive Polish victory.

A parliamentary democracy under the Small Constitution of 1919 gave way to the Sanacja regime after Józef Piłsudski's coup of May 1926; elections from 1930 were manipulated and opposition activists were sent to Bereza Kartuska prison.
Almost a third of its people belonged to minorities, and after Piłsudski's death in 1935 the government openly discriminated against Jewish and, to a lesser extent, Ukrainian and Belarusian citizens.
dyk: Neighbouring cities of the new republic had belonged to different empires, so there was no direct railway connection between Warsaw and Kraków until 1934, and the country began with five different currencies.
ev: The Regency Council announces the restoration of Polish independence on 7 October, and on 14 November transfers its authority to Józef Piłsudski as Chief of State
The Treaty of Versailles confirms the rebirth of Poland, and the Small Constitution of 1919 establishes a parliamentary democracy
The Polish–Soviet War, fought since 1919, ends in a decisive Polish victory
The eastern borders are settled diplomatically and recognised by the League of Nations
Prime Minister Władysław Grabski introduces the złoty, which brings the hyperinflation under control without foreign loans or aid
Piłsudski takes power in a military coup in May and establishes the Sanacja regime
An authoritarian constitution is approved in the spring, and Piłsudski dies shortly after
Germany and Slovakia invade on 1 September and the Soviet Union on 17 September, and organised resistance ends on 6 October after the Battle of Kock

f.founder: Józef Piłsudski, Chief of State from 14 November 1918, after the Regency Council announced the restoration of independence on 7 October 1918
f.predecessor: Kingdom of Poland (1917–1918) under the Regency Council; before it, the Austrian, Prussian and Russian partitions
f.successor: German and Soviet occupation (the General Government, lands incorporated into Nazi Germany and annexed to the Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic and the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic); the Polish government-in-exile and the Polish Underground State
